title: Allahabad HC Fines Builder Rs. 2.5 Lakh for Dragging Homebuyer Through 13 Years of Litigation
case_name: M/s Aims Max Gardenia Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. Mrs. Pratibha Gupta
card_summary: A homebuyer who booked a flat in Noida's Golf City project in 2011 never got possession despite RERA ordering it with 24% interest from June 2013, and a recovery certificate for about Rs. 41 lakh followed in 2019. The builder's appeal was dismissed for want of prosecution, twice restored on the same ground. The High Court imposed Rs. 2.5 lakh costs, holding the litigation defeated RERA's purpose of a quick remedy.
card_tip: A builder that keeps reviving a dismissed appeal rather than paying a recovery certificate risks costs for frivolous litigation on top of the underlying delay-interest liability.
verification_notes: The case name M/s Aims Max Gardenia Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. Mrs. Pratibha Gupta, the Golf City Sector 75 Noida project, the 2011 booking, the 24% delay interest from June 2013, the roughly Rs. 41.2 lakh recovery certificate, the dismissal for want of prosecution, and the Rs. 2.5 lakh costs are consistent across LiveLaw's and Outlook Money's reports. The exact date of the Appellate Tribunal's dismissal order was not confirmed in either report; the High Court's own costs order was reported on 8 August 2026.
